analysis.title: markets / macro: eight short observations on the current setup (Pasquariello, 20 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NVDA fell six straight weeks into Q3 earnings despite strong fundamentals and a large buyback. Market cap went from $415bn at the launch of ChatGPT to a recent high of $5.75tr and is $3.5tr today.
NDX sits in a notable technical position after a two-year bull uptrend. The note leaves the interpretation to the reader.

The GS US financial conditions index has tightened meaningfully in 2H 2026, driven by lower stocks and a stronger dollar. It is at its tightest level in 18 months. Pasquariello cares because he believes the Fed watches financial conditions closely.

A Fed tightening cycle is underway. Bulls have often died at the hands of central bankers (2018, 2022 cited). The bond market discounts another three hikes over the next year, and Pasquariello does not think equities are naive to that.

Open question: a modest hiking cycle that takes back earlier cuts, or a much harsher one. One camp believes the FOMC is behind the curve and fears the latter. GS economics expects core PCE to trend to 2.4% by end of next year, at which point hikes turn into cuts.

Hedge fund de-risking has approached extreme levels in magnitude and duration. Single stocks have been sold nine straight weeks and macro shorts covered four straight weeks. Equity L/S gross exposure is in the bottom quartile of the past year and net exposure is at the dead lows.
Client exposure to the momentum factor has dropped sharply. Momentum has been volatile in 2H 2026.

GS PB shows net selling of tech for six consecutive weeks. Hedge funds are the most underweight the sector in five years vs MSCI ACWI. CTAs have been significant sellers of NDX futures and hold a meaningful net short.
Two-thirds of S&P companies mentioned AI on their Q3 call, but only 3% quantified the impact of AI productivity on earnings.

S&P has gone nowhere in five months despite strong nominal GDP growth, earnings and inflows, and tech valuations keep compressing. The IT sector forward P/E fell from 24x to 16x over nine months while forward EPS rose 64%. In the nine months to the March 2000 peak, forward P/E rose from 34x to 48x on a 16% EPS gain.
Pasquariello reads the market as treating AI as a massive cyclical boom and as wary that earnings are currently above sustainable levels. He calls this the central story of recent weeks.

market_movers.rationale: Down six straight weeks into Q3 earnings. Ballast has not been found despite strong fundamentals and a large buyback.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge funds are the most underweight in five years, PB has net sold for six weeks and CTAs are net short NDX. The sector's forward P/E has compressed to 16x despite 64% EPS growth. The note states no formal rating.

earnings_insights: NVDA headed into Q3 earnings after six straight weekly declines. The note gives no reported or estimated figures.
S&P IT sector forward EPS rose 64% over the past nine months (Goldman Sachs FICC & Equities, Bloomberg, GIR, as of 19 Nov 2026). Forward P/E fell from 24x to 16x.
Two-thirds of S&P companies mentioned AI on their Q3 calls. Only 3% quantified the impact of AI productivity on earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: GS economics expects core PCE to trend to 2.4% by end of next year, at which point the hiking cycle becomes a cutting cycle. The bond market already discounts three more hikes.
tension_points.bear_case: A camp believes the FOMC is behind the curve and that the Fed will have to get properly rough. Bull markets ended under central bankers in 2018 and 2022.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core PCE failing to trend toward 2.4% by the end of next year, which would keep the hiking cycle going instead of turning into a cutting cycle.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech valuations keep compressing as hedge funds and CTAs cut exposure, and the market treats AI as a cyclical boom while wary of over-earning.
theme_stances.evidence: the market is far more sober today
